react_result.final_narrative_text: The treatment group exhibits a coordinated disruption of sulfur-amino-acid metabolism and interconnected one-carbon/trans-sulfuration pathways. Three independent enrichment paradigms — RaMP multi-database ORA, Mummichog m/z-network analysis, and MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA — converge on Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism (KEGG:hsa00260) as the top cross-paradigm winner, with a 711-fold fold-enrichment and FDR 3.9e-14 in RaMP, p=0.0037 in Mummichog (rank 1), and p=0.0108 in MetaboAnalystR. Six driver metabolites map to this pathway: L-methionine, S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine, L-cysteine, 2-oxobutanoate, L-ornithine, and (R)-lipoic acid, all confirmed in the method-specific hit rosters. Methionine and cysteine metabolism (KEGG:hsa00480) emerges as the strongest single-pathway signal in MetaboAnalystR (p=0.0002) and appears as a dedicated Mummichog module (rank 5, p=0.0304), covering L-methionine, S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine, L-cysteine, and 2-oxobutanoate. Arginine and proline metabolism (KEGG:hsa00330) is supported by MetaboAnalystR (p=0.0128) and Mummichog (rank 4, p=0.016), with L-ornithine and 1-pyrroline-5-carboxylic acid as the matching input metabolites — the latter is the cyclised form of L-glutamic 5-semialdehyde, directly linking the urea cycle to proline biosynthesis. Trans-sulfuration, one-carbon metabolism and related pathways (WP:WP2525) appears in RaMP (FDR 1.2e-11) and MetaboAnalystR (rank 2, p=0.0002), anchoring the methionine cycle to downstream cysteine generation and methylation homeostasis. The convergence of S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine (an SAM cycle intermediate), L-methionine, L-cysteine, and lipoic acid across these pathways points to a perturbation in methyl-group donor availability and oxidative thiol metabolism. Phenylephrine and 5,6-dihydroxyindole additionally map to the tyrosine metabolism network (Mummichog rank 3, p=0.006), suggesting secondary catecholamine pathway involvement.
